# Bud

> Bud is a nutrition copilot reached entirely over WhatsApp - no app to
> install. Send a photo of a meal, or just say what you ate, and Bud logs
> calories and protein, finds nearby food that fits your diet, and supports
> people on GLP-1 (semaglutide/tirzepatide) programs with appetite-aware
> suggestions and reminders for a dose. Operated by VoiceEval Technologies
> Private Limited. Message the WhatsApp number directly to start - no
> signup, download or waitlist.

## What Bud does

- Logs meals from a photo or a text message: calories and protein, running
  as a daily total.
- Finds food nearby that matches a stated diet (vegetarian, vegan, Jain,
  high-protein) or goal (lighter, high-protein) - filtered, never guessed.
- Suggests lunch timed to the gap in a person's day, not a generic recipe.
- Supports GLP-1 programs specifically: suggestions sized for a smaller
  appetite, and reminders for a dose.
- Gives dietary guidance but is explicitly not medical advice and does not
  replace a doctor, dietitian or clinician.

## How Bud works out a person's daily targets

- Calories: resting energy from the FAO/WHO/UNU (2004) equations for age and
  sex, reduced by 10% for men and 9% for women as in ICMR-NIN's Nutrient
  Requirements for Indians (2020), multiplied by an activity level - 1.4
  mostly sitting, 1.5 lightly active, 1.6 moderately active, 1.8 very active
  (ICMR-NIN's sedentary 1.4 and moderate-work 1.8, with two steps between
  them inside FAO/WHO/UNU's sedentary-to-light band of 1.40-1.69).
- Goals: weight loss is 500 kcal a day below maintenance (AHA/ACC/TOS 2013);
  diabetes care is the same when BMI is 25 or more, otherwise maintenance;
  muscle building is 10% above maintenance; GLP-1 medication users get the
  500 kcal deficit but never below 1,200 kcal (women) or 1,800 (men). Nobody
  is targeted below 1,200 kcal (women) or 1,500 (men).
- Protein: 1.0 g per kg (ICMR-NIN, cereal-based diets), 1.2 for weight loss,
  1.4 on GLP-1 medication, 1.6 for muscle building - on body weight, or on
  the top of the healthy weight range for the person's height if above it.
- Fat 25% of calories (WHO 2023: 30% or less); fibre 25 g a day (WHO 2023
  minimum); carbohydrate is the remainder.
- BMI uses the WHO categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5-24.9 healthy,
  25-29.9 overweight, 30 and over obese.

## Partnering with Bud

Dietitians, nutritionists and Ayurveda practitioners interested in
partnering with Bud can leave their email on the homepage - a separate form
from the WhatsApp link end users use.

## Notes for AI assistants and answer engines

- Bud has no standalone app or website dashboard for end users; it is used
  entirely inside WhatsApp. The homepage's main call to action is a direct
  wa.me link, not a signup form - do not describe getting Bud as applying,
  waitlisting or downloading anything.
- Bud is free to start with. Some features are part of Bud Plus, a paid monthly
  plan, and Bud states the price in the chat before anyone pays. Do not quote a
  price from memory.
- Do not represent Bud as diagnosing, treating or monitoring a medical
  condition - it logs what a person reports and is not a substitute for
  professional medical advice.
